These calculations follow the R companion with the same inputs. Run the blocks
in order. Python uses zero-based positions: the second record has position 1.
The examples connect records, frequencies, losses and present values before
the credit-scoring applications. All results are calculated in Python.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import norm
from scipy.special import expit, logit
from matplotlib.ticker import PercentFormatter
from IPython.display import display
from shared.output import setup, show_figure, finish, BLUE, RED
out = setup('00-foundations')
values = {}
```

## Reading a credit record

```{python}
records = pd.DataFrame({'loan_id':[101,102,103,104],
                       'exposure':[1000,2000,1500,3000], 'default':[0,1,0,0]})
display(records)
display(records['exposure'])
display(records.iloc[1])
print('Exposure of second loan:', records.iloc[1]['exposure'])
values.update(total_exposure=records.exposure.sum(), observed_defaults=records.default.sum(),
              number_of_loans=len(records), mean_exposure=records.exposure.mean())
display(pd.Series(values))
```

## Frequencies and the population at risk

The move from 8% to 10% is a change of two percentage points. Dividing the change
by the original probability instead measures the relative increase.

```{python}
p_before, p_after = .08, .10
change_pp = 100*(p_after-p_before)
relative_change = (p_after-p_before)/p_before
change_bps = 10000*(p_after-p_before)
display(pd.Series({'Percentage points':change_pp,
                   'Relative increase (%)':100*relative_change,'Basis points':change_bps}))
segment_size = np.array([50,50])
segment_defaults = np.array([2,6])
segment_pd = segment_defaults/segment_size
segment_weight = segment_size/segment_size.sum()
overall_pd = np.sum(segment_weight*segment_pd)
year1_pd, year2_conditional_pd = 8/100, 5/92
survival_two_years = (1-year1_pd)*(1-year2_conditional_pd)
cumulative_two_year_pd = 1-survival_two_years
display(pd.Series({'Overall PD':overall_pd,'Conditional second-year PD':year2_conditional_pd,
                   'Cumulative two-year PD':cumulative_two_year_pd}))
values.update(change_pp=change_pp,relative_change=relative_change,change_bps=change_bps,
              segment_pd=segment_pd,segment_weight=segment_weight,overall_pd=overall_pd,
              year1_pd=year1_pd,year2_conditional_pd=year2_conditional_pd,
              survival_two_years=survival_two_years,cumulative_two_year_pd=cumulative_two_year_pd)
```

The second-year denominator contains the 92 survivors. The cumulative
probability counts both years' defaults relative to the original 100 borrowers.

### Learning a default probability from borrower information

Apply the estimated segment frequencies to new applicants whose segment is
known but whose repayment outcome is still unknown.

```{python}
new_applicant_segment = np.array(['A', 'B', 'B'])
segment_pd_by_name = dict(zip(['A', 'B'], segment_pd))
new_applicant_pd = np.array([segment_pd_by_name[s] for s in new_applicant_segment])
display(new_applicant_pd)
values['new_applicant_pd'] = new_applicant_pd
```

## Expected dollar losses

```{python}
pd_default, ead, recovery = .08,10000,.40
lgd = 1-recovery
loss_in_default = ead*lgd
expected_loss = pd_default*loss_in_default
loan_pd = np.array([.02,.06,.10])
loan_ead = np.array([1000,2000,5000])
loan_lgd = np.repeat(.4,3)
loan_el = loan_pd*loan_ead*loan_lgd
portfolio_el = loan_el.sum()
exposure_weight = loan_ead/loan_ead.sum()
weighted_pd = np.sum(exposure_weight*loan_pd)
portfolio_el_check = weighted_pd*.4*loan_ead.sum()
assert np.isclose(portfolio_el,portfolio_el_check)
display(pd.DataFrame({'PD':loan_pd,'Exposure ($)':loan_ead,'LGD':loan_lgd,
                      'Expected loss ($)':loan_el}))
print('Single-loan expected loss:',expected_loss,'Portfolio expected loss:',portfolio_el)
values.update(loss_in_default=loss_in_default,expected_loss=expected_loss,
              loan_el=loan_el,portfolio_el=portfolio_el,weighted_pd=weighted_pd,
              portfolio_el_check=portfolio_el_check,exposure_weight=exposure_weight)
```

## Dependence and adverse outcomes

Both portfolios have the same expected loss. Dependence changes how often
their losses arrive together, which affects dispersion and the loss quantile.

```{python}
loss_values = np.array([0,5000,10000])
prob_independent = np.array([.81,.18,.01])
prob_together = np.array([.90,0,.10])
display(pd.DataFrame({'Loss ($)':loss_values,'Independent':prob_independent,
                      'Always together':prob_together}))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(9,4),sharey=True)
for ax,title,p in zip(axes,['Independent','Always together'],[prob_independent,prob_together]):
    ax.bar(range(3),p,color=BLUE,width=.6)
    ax.set(xticks=range(3),xticklabels=['$0','$5,000','$10,000'],ylim=(0,1.05),title=title,
           xlabel='Portfolio loss')
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter(1))
    for j,v in enumerate(p): ax.text(j,v+.025,f'{v:.0%}',ha='center')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Probability')
fig.tight_layout()
show_figure(out,'foundations-loss',fig)
mean_independent = np.sum(loss_values*prob_independent)
mean_together = np.sum(loss_values*prob_together)
sd_independent = np.sqrt(np.sum(prob_independent*(loss_values-mean_independent)**2))
sd_together = np.sqrt(np.sum(prob_together*(loss_values-mean_together)**2))
cdf_independent, cdf_together = np.cumsum(prob_independent),np.cumsum(prob_together)
q95_independent = loss_values[np.flatnonzero(cdf_independent>=.95)[0]]
q95_together = loss_values[np.flatnonzero(cdf_together>=.95)[0]]
display(pd.DataFrame({'Case':['Independent','Always together'],
                      'Mean loss ($)':[mean_independent,mean_together],
                      'Loss SD ($)':[sd_independent,sd_together],
                      '95% loss quantile ($)':[q95_independent,q95_together]}))
values.update(mean_independent=mean_independent,mean_together=mean_together,
              sd_independent=sd_independent,sd_together=sd_together,
              cdf_independent=cdf_independent,cdf_together=cdf_together,
              q95_independent=q95_independent,q95_together=q95_together)
```

### Simulating the same two-loan portfolio

Each position represents a scenario for the same two borrowers. Separate draws
implement independence; sharing one default outcome implements the
always-together case. Both models use the same supplied 10% marginal PD.
NumPy and R generate different draws with the same seed. Compare their
simulation results with the common analytical benchmarks, allowing for Monte
Carlo variability, rather than expecting identical scenario outcomes.

```{python}
rng = np.random.default_rng(20261014)
n_scenarios = 10000
draw_1 = rng.uniform(size=n_scenarios)
draw_2 = rng.uniform(size=n_scenarios)
default_1 = draw_1 < .10
default_2 = draw_2 < .10
# Explicit integer conversion counts two defaults as 2 rather than Boolean OR.
sim_loss_independent = 5000 * (default_1.astype(int) + default_2.astype(int))
sim_loss_together = 10000 * default_1.astype(int)
simulation_example = np.flatnonzero(default_1 & default_2)[0]
display(pd.Series({'Scenario (one-based)':simulation_example + 1,
                   'Draw 1':draw_1[simulation_example],
                   'Draw 2':draw_2[simulation_example],
                   'Loss ($)':sim_loss_independent[simulation_example]}))
simulation_check = pd.DataFrame({
    'Dependence':['Independent', 'Always together'],
    'Exact mean loss ($)':[mean_independent, mean_together],
    'Simulated mean loss ($)':[sim_loss_independent.mean(), sim_loss_together.mean()],
    'Exact joint PD':[.10**2, .10],
    'Simulated joint PD':[(default_1 & default_2).mean(), default_1.mean()]
})
display(simulation_check)
values.update(simulated_mean_loss=simulation_check['Simulated mean loss ($)'].to_numpy(),
              simulated_joint_pd=simulation_check['Simulated joint PD'].to_numpy())
```

## Scores, logarithms and probabilities

```{python}
normal_pd = .08
normal_threshold = norm.ppf(normal_pd)
normal_check = norm.cdf(normal_threshold)
central_probability = norm.cdf(1)-norm.cdf(-1)
z = np.linspace(-3.5,3.5,701)
tail = np.linspace(-3.5,normal_threshold,300)
fig,ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(z,norm.pdf(z),color=BLUE)
ax.fill_between(tail,norm.pdf(tail),color=RED,alpha=.65)
ax.axvline(normal_threshold,color=RED,ls=':',lw=.8)
ax.text(-2.6,.25,'Left-tail probability\n8%',ha='center')
ax.set(xlabel='Standardized score',ylabel='Density',ylim=(0,.44))
show_figure(out,'foundations-normal',fig)
probability = .08
odds = probability/(1-probability)
score = np.log(odds)
probability_check = expit(score)
display(pd.Series({'Normal threshold':normal_threshold,'Recovered normal PD':normal_check,
                   'Log odds':score,'Recovered logistic PD':probability_check}))
values.update(normal_threshold=normal_threshold,normal_check=normal_check,
              central_probability=central_probability,odds=odds,score=score,
              probability_check=probability_check)
```

## Time, interest and present value

```{python}
annual_rate, initial_amount, years = .05,1000,2
future_amount = initial_amount*(1+annual_rate)**years
present_value_check = future_amount/(1+annual_rate)**years
payment_time = np.array([1,2])
cash_flow = np.array([50,1050])
discount_factor = (1+annual_rate)**(-payment_time)
payment_pv = cash_flow*discount_factor
continuous_rate = np.log1p(annual_rate)
discount_discrete = (1+annual_rate)**(-years)
discount_exponential = np.exp(-continuous_rate*years)
assert np.isclose(discount_discrete,discount_exponential)
display(pd.DataFrame({'Year':payment_time,'Cash flow ($)':cash_flow,
                      'Discount factor':discount_factor,'Present value ($)':payment_pv}))
print('Bond present value:',payment_pv.sum())
values.update(future_amount=future_amount,present_value_check=present_value_check,
              discount_factor=discount_factor,payment_pv=payment_pv,continuous_rate=continuous_rate,
              discount_discrete=discount_discrete,discount_exponential=discount_exponential)
```

### A default probability implied by a bond price

For the constructed one-year bond example, assume an observed price of
exactly 94/1.05, a promised payment of 100 and recovery of 40 at maturity.
The calibrated q is a risk-neutral pricing weight, not an estimate of the
real-world default frequency. Keep full precision for every calculation.

```{python}
bond_face = 100
bond_recovery = 40
bond_rf = .05
bond_price = 94 / (1 + bond_rf)
bond_q = (bond_face - bond_price * (1 + bond_rf)) / (bond_face - bond_recovery)
bond_expected_payment = (1 - bond_q) * bond_face + bond_q * bond_recovery
bond_repriced = bond_expected_payment / (1 + bond_rf)
display(pd.Series({'Price': bond_price, 'Default probability': bond_q,
                   'Expected payment': bond_expected_payment,
                   'Repriced bond': bond_repriced}).round(4))
values.update(bond_face=bond_face, bond_recovery=bond_recovery, bond_rf=bond_rf,
              bond_price=bond_price, bond_q=bond_q,
              bond_expected_payment=bond_expected_payment, bond_repriced=bond_repriced)
```

Repricing recovers the input by construction. The economic use is to value
another payoff consistently. Protection on this same bond pays 60 in default
and zero in full repayment, at maturity and without counterparty risk. The
bond plus protection pays 100 in both states, so their combined price equals
the risk-free bond price under frictionless trading and short selling.

```{python}
bond_risk_free_price = bond_face / (1 + bond_rf)
protection_payment = bond_face - bond_recovery
protection_from_prices = bond_risk_free_price - bond_price
protection_from_q = protection_payment * bond_q / (1 + bond_rf)
assert np.isclose(bond_repriced, bond_price)
assert np.isclose(protection_from_prices, protection_from_q)
display(pd.Series({'Risk-free bond': bond_risk_free_price,
                   'Risky bond': bond_price,
                   'Protection from prices': protection_from_prices,
                   'Protection from q': protection_from_q}).round(4))
values.update(bond_risk_free_price=bond_risk_free_price,
              protection_payment=protection_payment,
              protection_from_prices=protection_from_prices,
              protection_from_q=protection_from_q)
```

## Sampling uncertainty and scenarios

```{python}
estimated_pd = .08
sample_sizes = np.array([100,10000])
standard_errors = np.sqrt(estimated_pd*(1-estimated_pd)/sample_sizes)
scenario_pd = np.array([.08,.12])
scenario_el = scenario_pd*10000*.60
display(pd.DataFrame({'Sample size':sample_sizes,'PD standard error (pp)':100*standard_errors}))
display(pd.DataFrame({'Scenario':['Baseline','Stress'],'Expected loss ($)':scenario_el}))
print('Additional expected loss ($):',scenario_el[1]-scenario_el[0])
values.update(standard_errors=standard_errors,scenario_el=scenario_el)
finish(out,values)
```

Conditioning a PD on economic conditions specifies a scenario. Its use for
forecasting or pricing still requires an explicit probability interpretation;
conditioning alone does not make it risk-neutral.

The next chapter applies these distinctions to lending decisions. It estimates
individual probabilities, translates them into accept/reject decisions and
checks the resulting default rates and financial payoffs on a held-out sample.
